title: Captured Images thumbnails are inert — tapping a frame does nothing anywhere in Analytics
reasoning: Code contains the claim. image_thumbnail_strip.dart:417-419 wires InkWell.onTap to _handleTap (line 717), which honours a caller-supplied onImageTap and otherwise calls showFrameDetailDialog; frame_detail_dialog.dart and frame_thumbnail_loader.dart both exist as described. The fix is at the widget, not at the two call sites, so both existing callers (session_tab.dart:391, session_detail_dialog.dart:299 — neither passes a handler) and any future caller get the inspector. Checked the two adversarial angles that could have made this hollow: (a) the invalidate after an accept/reject is ref.invalidate(dbSessionImagesProvider) on the whole FAMILY, and session_detail_dialog watches dbSessionImagesProvider(session.id) — so the detail dialog's own rail does refresh, not just the session tab's; (b) the 'solvedRa is HOURS' claim is independently corroborated (apps/desktop/lib/headless_api/handlers/session_handlers.dart:355 validates solvedRa with min:0 max:24, centering_service.dart:1124 writes solvedRa: solvedRaHours, and photometric_calibration_wizard/star_matching.dart:312 passes image.solvedRa as raHours), so formatRaHms is correct and not a new units bug. Accept/reject in the inspector goes through imagingRecordsRepositoryProvider, which branches to the remote host in NetworkBackend mode (imaging_records_repository.dart:370), so the remote-mode claim is real. Note: the new class shares the name FrameDetailDialog with an unrelated sequencer dialog at screens/sequencer/widgets/run_dashboard/frame_detail_dialog.dart — no library imports both, so it compiles and is only a naming nit.
evidence: Test packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/analytics/widgets/thumbnail_rail_reachable_test.dart: 6/6 pass. SEVER: replaced the showFrameDetailDialog(...) call inside _handleTap with a constant, reran — 'tapping a thumbnail opens the frame inspector' went RED (00:00 +2 -1) while the other five stayed green; restored and re-ran to green. The test therefore fails on the production wiring, not just on internal logic. Re-checked in this pass: image_thumbnail_strip.dart:717-731 _handleTap honours widget.onImageTap and otherwise calls showFrameDetailDialog; both production call sites (session_detail_dialog.dart:299, session_tab.dart:391) still pass no handler, so both inherit the inspector.

title: Equipment Stats: half of the tab is permanently "Not tracked"
reasoning: Code contains the claim and then some. equipment_stats.dart now watches sequenceRunsProvider and folds ParsedRunStats.meridianFlips across every run (lines 38-49), with _parseRunStats swallowing FormatException/TypeError so one bad blob contributes zero. The write path is real, not assumed: sequence_stats_provider.dart:162 recordMeridianFlip() is called from sequence_executor/event_operations.dart:1022 on a 'success' flip outcome and persisted into sequence_runs.statsJson. sequenceRunsProvider polls the host's /api/sequence-runs under NetworkBackend, so the slave claim is true. The summary UNDERSTATES what shipped: the other five rows (Total Slews, Total Tracking Time, Total Movements, Total Guide Time, Star Lost Events) were not 'left' — they were deleted along with the _kNotTracked constant, which is a stronger fix than described and matches the finding. Residual worth recording, not a refutation: _incrementRunStat returns early when liveSequenceStatsProvider is null, and MeridianFlipStandaloneMonitor only fires when no sequence is running (meridian_flip_provider.dart:635-640), so a flip performed by the standalone monitor or the manual Equipment-screen command is recorded nowhere in the schema and never reaches this total. sequence_runs.statsJson is the only persistent flip record in the DB. So the row is an in-sequence flip count presented as an all-time one; it undercounts for a standalone-only operator. That gap needs a new persistence path in shared core code, so I did not edit it.
evidence: Test packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/analytics/equipment_stats_meridian_flips_test.dart: 2/2 pass. SEVER: reverted the Mount row to a const _Stat(value: 'Not tracked') — 'Meridian Flips totals the count the runs recorded' went RED immediately (00:00 +0 -1); restored to green. Corrupt-blob case is covered by the test ('not json' and '{}' rows contribute 0 without taking the tab down). Re-checked in this pass: the file is packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/analytics/analytics_screen/equipment_stats.dart — line 38 watches sequenceRunsProvider, 45-46 folds ParsedRunStats.meridianFlips through a null-tolerant _parseRunStats, and line 173 renders it as the Meridian Flips stat.

title: Science tab defaults to the newest session even when it has no science data
reasoning: The code contains the claim. science_analytics_tab.dart:81-95 defines latestScienceProductSessionProvider (union of ScienceDao.getSessionIdsWithPhotometry and ImagesDao.getSessionIdsWithSolvedFrames, walked in allSessionsProvider order, newest first) and the build method at line 316-320 resolves manual pick -> live -> product session -> light-frame session -> newest, exactly as described. Both DAO methods really exist and are real drift queries (science_dao.dart:122 on photometryMeasurements.sessionId; images_dao.dart:185 on capturedImages.isPlateSolved). What was INCOMPLETE is the guard, in precisely the shape this campaign has been catching: all four shipped tests read latestScienceProductSessionProvider directly out of a ProviderContainer and never pump the tab, so the fix's entire production wiring can be deleted with the suite green — I deleted the line and got 4/4 passing. Two smaller notes, neither a refutation: (a) on NetworkBackend the provider returns null exactly like its predecessor, so a slave still opens on the newest session with light frames — the summary does not claim otherwise, but the fix does not reach remote mode; (b) both session-id providers are async, so the first frame legitimately falls through to allSessions.first before settling on the product session — I observed the tab query session 5 then session 4, so there is a one-frame flash of the wrong night. Pre-existing and inherent to the fallback chain, not introduced here.
repairSummary: Added a widget-level test to packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/analytics/widgets/science_default_session_test.dart ('the tab itself analyses the science-product session') that pumps the real ScienceAnalyticsTab with latestScienceProductSessionProvider=4 and latestScienceSessionProvider=5 and records every session id the tab passes to sessionPhotometryProvider, asserting the settled choice is 4. It observes the tab's own call site rather than the provider it is supposed to consult, so it is red whenever the wiring is cut, whichever render branch the tab takes.
evidence: SEVER (before repair): removed 'ref.watch(latestScienceProductSessionProvider).valueOrNull ??' from science_analytics_tab.dart:318 — all 4 existing tests still PASSED (00:00 +4: All tests passed!), proving the guard was hollow. SEVER (after repair): same cut, new test went RED with 'Expected: <4> Actual: <5>' (00:00 +4 -1); restored the line and the file is 5/5 green.

title: Science report timestamps are printed without a timezone, so a shared report is ambiguous by up to a day
reasoning: The code contains the claim exactly. science_report_exporter.dart:146 defines `_utcStamp(DateTime when) => when.toUtc().toIso8601String()` and lines 159/161 print '- **Started (UTC):**' / '- **Ended (UTC):**' through it. I enumerated every DateTime print in the file: the footer (line 112) and the export filename (127) already stamped UTC, the light-curve block (257-289) already called .toUtc() before formatting, and there are no other instants in the markdown — so 'only the Session block was wrong' is true rather than convenient. Wall-clock duration (163) is a difference, unaffected by the conversion. Worth recording but NOT a refutation of this item: the same ambiguity still exists in the sibling non-science exporters — session_export_service.dart:304 ('Started: ${session.startTime}', bare toString, not even ISO shaped) and session_report_service.dart:528/719 — which are a different report and a separate finding. The fix shipped NO test, which is why I added one.
repairSummary: Added 'session start/end are printed as labelled UTC instants' to packages/skotiq_core/test/services/science/science_report_exporter_test.dart. It asserts the exact label plus the exact UTC instant and asserts the old unlabelled '- **Started:**' / '- **Ended:**' forms are absent, so it is decisive even on a machine whose local zone is already UTC (where a naive round-trip assertion would be vacuous).
evidence: SEVER: rewrote lines 159/161 back to '- **Started:** ${session.startTime.toIso8601String()}' / '- **Ended:** ...' — the new test went RED (00:00 +4 -1) while the other four stayed green; restored, 5/5 green. skotiq_core science_report_exporter_test.dart: 5/5 pass.

title: Every science rung sheet is a dead end: it names the blocker but gives no button to clear it
reasoning: The mechanism shipped as described — science_rung_sheet.dart:14-15/41-50 takes unlockLabel/onUnlock and the locked branch (line 122-137) renders a second button beside 'Got it' — and it was tested. What it was wired TO is the problem. science_ladder_card.dart:176 bound onUnlock to `onJumpToPhotometry`, and on the Science tab's POPULATED branch that callback is `_jumpTo(_sectionKeys.photometry)` (science_analytics_tab.dart:653) — a scroll to the PHOTOMETRY section, which is an empty Differential Photometry chart card plus export buttons (lines 788-830). It cannot track a star. The file says so itself twelve lines away, at science_analytics_tab.dart:660-663: 'Rung 2 says Pick a target; the PHOTOMETRY section it used to scroll to plots curves and exports them, it does not choose the star' — an EARLIER fix in this same campaign moved rung 2's CTA off that section for precisely this reason, and this fix routed the unlock straight back to it. So for the commonest locked case (a night of plate-solved frames and no photometry: allEmpty is false, so the populated branch renders, and rung 3 'Build a light curve' is locked) the sheet's dead end became a scroll to a dead end one screen further down. It happened to work on the empty branch, where onJumpToPhotometry is `_goPickPhotometryTarget` — the branch the shipped test's single fake callback models — which is why the test did not catch it. The summary's load-bearing claim, 'all three lockable prerequisites are satisfied in the photometry section', is false on the branch that matters.
repairSummary: science_ladder_card.dart _openRung now binds onUnlock to `onPickTarget` and labels it 'Open Science HUD'. onPickTarget is `_goPickPhotometryTarget` on BOTH branches of the Science tab (science_analytics_tab.dart:606 and :663) — it opens the Science HUD on the imaging screen, which is the only control in the app that picks a photometry target and the place all three lockable prerequisites (track a star, gather ten points, record something exportable) are actually cleared. Rewrote science_rung_unlock_test.dart to pass DISTINCT fakes for onPickTarget and onJumpToPhotometry and assert the unlock fires the former and never the latter — the previous single-fake shape could not tell the two destinations apart — and added a fourth case proving a never-locked rung still offers no unlock.
evidence: Tests: science_rung_unlock_test.dart 4/4 pass; the four ladder/rung suites together (rung_unlock, ladder_pick_target, ladder_run_calibration, ladder_evidence, ladder_model) 31/31 pass, no regressions. SEVER: set unlockLabel/onUnlock back to null — 2 of the 4 went RED (00:00 +2 -2), including the new 'scrolledToCharts, 0' assertion's test; restored to 4/4. The old test would also have passed against the relocated wiring, which is how it shipped.

title: 3D Surface Explorer has no axes, no colour scale and no numbers, so the plot cannot be read
reasoning: All three additions are in the file and all three are wired. (1) Corner tags: _SurfacePainter.paint (science_surface_explorer.dart:716-750) projects the four grid corners and draws 'r<row>·c<col>' with the same `project` closure as the markers, clamped inside the canvas. The 'tile_row/tile_col are the image row/column' claim is independently true: native/skotiq_native/bridge/src/api/imaging.rs:2168 sets tile_row = row / tile_col = col inside `for y in y_start..y_end { for x in x_start..x_end`, so row is the y band and col the x band. (2) Colour bar: _ValueScaleBar prints scale.low/high on the ramp ends, plus median, the true min-max and the saturation note. The unit table is honest against the producer, which I checked rather than assumed — imaging.rs:2151 computes clip_low/clip_high as `100.0 * count / count_f64` (so '%'), background is the tile p50 of pixel values (so ' ADU'), uniformity is a coefficient of variation and snr a ratio (so no unit, correctly left blank). (3) Tap-to-read: _selectTileAt resolves against projectSurfaceTiles with the SAME low/high the painter uses (both call surfaceValueScale on the same selectedTiles), so the hit test and the drawing cannot drift apart; >18px clears the readout; the layer dropdown clears _selectedTile so one layer's value is never printed under another's name. The 16:9-up-to-300px cap is at line 371-378. Two honest limits: the corner tags shipped with NO test of any kind (fixed below), and 'fwhm'/'hfr'/'residual_mag' units are asserted for layer types this Rust function does not emit — they exist in ScienceLayerType and the units are conventional, but I could not point at a producer, so that third of the unit table is unverified rather than wrong.
repairSummary: Added coverage, not a behaviour change: 'the painter tags all four grid corners on the surface' in science_surface_explorer_readable_test.dart drives the live CustomPainter through a Canvas that records drawParagraph offsets, asserts exactly four tags, and asserts each one lands within 40px of the corner it names as computed by projectSurfaceTiles. Nothing in the widget tree can see painted text, so this was the only way to guard the half of the fix that says WHERE.
evidence: science_surface_explorer_readable_test.dart 6/6 pass; with science_surface_contours_test.dart 9/9. SEVER 1: replaced the GestureDetector's onTapUp with null — 'tapping a marker names its tile and value' went RED (00:00 +4 -1). SEVER 2: skipped the corner-label loop body — the new painter test went RED with 'Expected: an object with length of <4> Actual: []' while the other five stayed green. Both restored; suite green.
